llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, cogito_8b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0905 (median 0) and met the 75 % coverage threshold on just two instances, indicating that virtually all responses failed to satisfy the ground‑truth requirements. The failure analysis shows that 498 tasks (99.6 %) were diagnosed as erroneous, with the most frequent root cause being *no_tool_use* (194 cases, 38.8 % of failures), followed by early termination (114) and task misunderstanding (113). Although the model performed 227 successful tool calls (45.6 % of the total tasks), the larger share of errors stemmed from purely cognitive missteps—271 tasks (54.4 %) where the model either stopped prematurely or answered without invoking any MCP tools. This pattern suggests that the model’s internal decision‑making does not reliably trigger the required tool‑use workflow, even when the tooling infrastructure is fully functional (zero sandbox or endpoint errors). A concrete remediation would be to augment the fine‑tuning data with explicit “tool‑first” exemplars and enforce a hard constraint in the prompting layer that blocks final answer generation until at least one tool call has returned valid data. Compared with other evaluated models, cogito_8b_output’s failure profile is distinguished by an unusually high proportion of *no_tool_use* and early‑termination errors rather than tool execution faults, indicating that the bottleneck lies in the model’s ability to recognize when external information is needed.
